method: order-swapped Jev pairwise comparisons, stable merge sort, Bradley-Terry fit (issue #301)
brief: The reader builds a search for Pokemon VGC (Regulation M-B) teams that beat the current top-50 meta teams. A discrete (masked) diffusion model writes whole six-Pokemon teams, conditioned on an asked win rate, and a search loop battles candidates with a behaviour-cloning policy to label them. Open problems: getting win rate to follow the ask, keeping teams diverse and novel, guidance strength, training labels from noisy battles, and planning which papers to read. The reader learns by working problems and prefers blogs before papers. Rank closest to the search itself first: building teams or decks in games, finding candidates beyond the training data, novelty and diversity of what a generator proposes, and judging or battling candidates. Diffusion technique ranks next when it changes how the ask steers generation; general machine-learning theory and workflow advice rank below both (owner picks, 2026-11-11: Q-DeckRec and Verifier-Constrained Flow Expansion over diffusion-guidance papers). Judge each option on two things: after its abstract, does it have a future for the counter-team search; and while reading, how much of it would be new to someone who already knows masked discrete diffusion, classifier-free guidance, quality diversity and black-box optimisation.
